absent: Signal dequeue, handler invocation and delivery to user context beyond queueing and wakeup
Callers and required execution context for internal send helper beyond sighand lock ownership
Full layouts, sizes and offsets for task, signal, sighand and pending structures
Scheduler wakeup mechanics and stopped-state transitions behind wake helpers
Audit, filesystem and permission implementations referenced by queue open path
Construction, update and lifetime of identifier maps and namespace relationships
Timer subsystem creation and expiry beyond ignored-signal handling
Tracepoint definitions and monitoring effects for generation outcomes
Signalfd notification mechanics beyond invocation on delivery
Group stop accounting and parent notification delivery beyond flag updates

findings.text: Dossier-visible helpers adjust and release per-user pending-signal accounting across nested user namespaces, with failure indicated by null return on acquisition.
Dossier-visible job control helpers set pending stop and trap marks, clear selected marks with consume semantics for stop, and release trapping waiters with ordered wakeup.

Dossier-visible identity mapping helpers translate kernel user identifiers to namespace-visible values, with munged variant substituting overflow identity on mapping failure and range helpers locating covering extents.
Dossier-visible utilities acquire sighand ownership under contention and classify signal payload layout from signal and code for downstream handling.
Message queue open entry validates name, creates or opens backing file with mode and attribute handling, and returns descriptor with write-hold lifecycle management.
Sighand acquisition entry provides safe access to mutable signal handling state for threads undergoing exit or rethreading, returning null when detached.
Group-scoped deliveries target shared pending state while process-private deliveries target per-task pending state.
Standard signals already marked pending are treated as already queued and do not allocate additional queue nodes.
Deliveries for SIGKILL and for tasks flagged PF_KTHREAD mark pending and notify without allocating info nodes.
When allocation fails, real-time signals from queueing paths report EAGAIN while other paths still mark delivery but discard detailed info.

Pending-signal accounting increments limits along the user-namespace chain under read-side protection, honors override for privileged origins, and rejects when exceeding configured maximum with drop notice.
Release of pending-signal accounting decrements along the chain, warns on underflow, and drops namespace references when counts reach empty.
Blocked signals are never deemed ignored, and traced tasks observe signals other than SIGKILL regardless of handler disposition.

Global init discards kernel-only signals, tasks flagged SIGNAL_UNKILLABLE ignore default SIG_DFL unless forced, tasks flagged PF_KTHREAD with SIG_KTHREAD_KERNEL require force, and SIG_IGN plus default-ignored are honored.
Tasks inside group exit drop signals generally, permitting SIGKILL during core dump collection.
Stop signals purge pending continue marks across shared and per-task queues, while continue purges stop marks, clears stop pending state, and wakes stopped tasks or notifies seized tracers.
A thread is eligible for wakeup when unblocked for the signal, not exiting, responsive rather than stopped or traced except for SIGKILL, and running or without pending signals.
Fatal signals directed at unblocked killable threads initiate group-wide exit, clear job control pending marks, force termination marks on member queues, and wake members.
Wakeup prefers the hinted thread when eligible, otherwise scans the group round-robin from cached target, leaving delivery queued for later observation when immediate wakeup is unnecessary.
Exiting tasks accept group-scoped signals for queueing but decline process-private scope.
Upward identifier translation yields failure sentinel when uncovered, with munged wrapper mapping sentinel to overflow identity.
Extent lookup succeeds only when the requested range lies fully inside the same extent, using linear scan for compact maps and ordered search for large maps.
Kill, child-status and real-time layouts are treated as carrying originator identity while timer, poll, fault variants and system layouts are not.
Fault layout refines bus, segmentation, trap and architecture-specific codes into dedicated sub-layouts, with timer and poll codes mapped from reserved negative values.
Multiprocess-scoped signals also update delayed collections, maintaining mutual exclusion between stop and continue marks.
Queue creation requires O_CREAT on absent entries and read-only state blocks creation, while existing entries reject O_EXCL and validate O_ACCMODE before permission check.
Timeout preparation reports EFAULT on faulty user copy and EINVAL on invalid time values.
Sighand lock ownership is required for queued-signal mutation, queue flushing, exit-scope checks and trap notification paths.

Sighand acquisition uses read-side critical section with IRQ-safe spinlocking, revalidates the pointer after locking, retries on concurrent detach or rethread, and treats null as detached with ordering barrier.
Credential and ucount accesses during accounting and identity stamping occur under read-side protection.
Extent reads rely on read barrier for stable view, and trapping release uses full barrier before waiter wakeup.
Queued signal node links into pending lists and carries disposition flags, accounting reference and info payload with originator fields.
Pending state combines a signal mask with a list of info nodes, with shared instance for group scope and per-task instance for private scope.
Identifier map stores extent count with inline storage for compact tables and separate ordered storage for larger tables.
Continue handling updates stop-related flags to record stopped versus interrupted stop, resets stop accounting, and defers parent notification until stop return observes the marks.
Job control marks transition among pending, consumed and dequeued conditions, with trapping bit coordinating waiter wakeup and trap notification for seized tasks.

Timer-originated queue nodes follow distinct release paths for ignored signals, with periodic valid timers moved to ignored tracking and other cases releasing references. Some builds provide empty handling.
Signal generation distinguishes ignored, already pending, delivered, overflow failure and info-loss outcomes for tracing.
Queue open proceeds through name lookup, create-or-open decision with audit and permission handling, file instantiation, and descriptor allocation with mount write-hold cleanup.
Allocation failure on non-queueing paths still marks delivery while discarding info, creating silent loss of origin details.
Concurrent increment and unwind paths guard against negative counts and overflow beyond allowed maximum, warning on underflow.
Sighand memory may be freed and reused during acquisition, mitigated by type-stable allocation and pointer revalidation under lock.
Pending-limit exhaustion emits a gated and rate-limited diagnostic tied to fatal-signal reporting controls.
Fatal signals that would otherwise start group exit are withheld from immediate group teardown when the target is traced, except for SIGKILL.
Standard versus real-time signal behavior pivots on SIGRTMIN, governing coalescing, allocation override and failure handling.
SEND_SIG_NOINFO and SEND_SIG_PRIV denote kernel-generated signals with distinct stamping of originator identity and SI_USER versus SI_KERNEL codes.
SIGCONT and kernel stop signals form an exclusive set governed by SIG_KERNEL_STOP_MASK and SIGCONT mask handling.
JOBCTL_PENDING_MASK, JOBCTL_STOP_PENDING, JOBCTL_STOP_CONSUME, JOBCTL_STOP_DEQUEUED, JOBCTL_STOP_SIGMASK, JOBCTL_TRAPPING and JOBCTL_LISTENING define pending, consumption and notification bits.
UCOUNT_RLIMIT_SIGPENDING with RLIMIT_SIGPENDING bounds pending queueing, while SI_TIMER, SI_SIGIO, SI_USER and SI_KERNEL distinguish timer, poll and origin classes.
